intro.en: Business vocabulary: companies and their people, the market, and how a product is sold.

texto.en:
**The company.** **Una empresa** can be **una multinacional** or **una pyme** (pequeña y mediana empresa). It has **una sede** (headquarters) and **sucursales**. It is run by **la dirección** and owned by **los socios** or **los accionistas**. **El empresario** is the owner or employer. Running it is **la gestión**.

**The market.** **La oferta y la demanda.** **El consumo.** **La competencia** is the other companies: **hacer la competencia a** alguien. A business is **rentable** when it gives **beneficios**; if not, it has **pérdidas** and may **quebrar** or **cerrar**.

**Buying and selling.** A shop **hace un pedido** to **un proveedor**, who sends **la mercancía**. Then come **la factura**, **el pago** and **la entrega**. Abroad: **exportar**, **importar**, **el comercio exterior**.

**Selling a new product.** First **un estudio de mercado**. Then **el lanzamiento**, with **una campaña publicitaria**: **anuncios**, **carteles**, **folletos**. The aim is that the public recognises **la marca**. A product **está de oferta** or **en promoción**.

**Useful verbs.** **Fundar** una empresa, **dirigir**, **gestionar**, **invertir en**, **contratar**, **negociar**, **firmar** un acuerdo, **lanzar** un producto, **crecer**, **estar en crisis**.

**False friends.** **La competencia** is competition between companies; a sports competition is **una competición**. **Un compromiso** is a commitment. **El éxito** is success, and an exit is **una salida**.

titulo.en: From a garage to forty countries

frases.es: La empresa nació en un garaje de Alicante, fundada por dos socios que no tenían más capital que sus ahorros.
frases.en: The company was born in a garage in Alicante, founded by two partners who had no capital other than their savings.
analisis: que no tenían más capital que sus ahorros

frases.es: Fabricaban zapatillas con plástico reciclado, un producto para el que, según el estudio de mercado, apenas había demanda.
frases.en: They made trainers from recycled plastic, a product for which, according to the market research, there was hardly any demand.

frases.es: Durante dos años tuvieron pérdidas y estuvieron a punto de quebrar.
frases.en: For two years they made losses and were on the verge of going bankrupt.

frases.es: Todo cambió cuando una actriz conocida apareció en una revista con un par que le habían regalado.
frases.en: Everything changed when a well-known actress appeared in a magazine wearing a pair she had been given.

frases.es: En una semana recibieron más pedidos de los que podían atender, sin haber gastado un euro en publicidad.
frases.en: In a week they received more orders than they could handle, without having spent a euro on advertising.
analisis: más pedidos de los que podían atender

frases.es: Hoy la marca vende en cuarenta países, tiene sucursales en tres continentes y sigue teniendo su sede en Alicante.
frases.en: Today the brand sells in forty countries, has branches on three continents and still has its headquarters in Alicante.

frases.es: Sus fundadores reconocen que, si hubieran hecho caso al estudio de mercado, nunca habrían lanzado el producto.
frases.en: Its founders admit that, if they had paid attention to the market research, they would never have launched the product.

pregunta.en: According to the text, what did the market research say?

A new partner with capital.en: The text does not say that.

bloques.correcta: A famous actress wore the trainers in a magazine

a skill.en: It can mean that elsewhere, but not in this context.

pregunta.en: Complete: more orders than they could handle.

de los que.en: Before a verb, de + article + que, agreeing with pedidos.

que.en: Before a verb you need de los que.

de lo que.en: With a noun, the article agrees: de los que.

texto.en: The company has its headquarters in Bilbao.
The company has its thirst in Bilbao.
The company has a branch in Bilbao.

traduccion.en: We placed an order with the supplier last week.

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write the business plan in summary for a small company you would like to set up: product, customers, competition and costs.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Present your business idea aloud to possible investors in three minutes.
